This is the collection point for tracking work items and development.,https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/,Medium,,Zackary Oleitschuk,712020:c79871b4-3321-48a4-b4ae-d1a84eb31c0b,Scott Drennan,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,Scott Drennan,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,08/Sep/25 7:28 AM,08/Sep/25 7:28 AM,,,,,,Platform Management,Terraform Scripting,,,,,,0,,,,,"I need to define Service Principals to run workspace admin tasks in each workspace, as well as an SP in each workspace that can be provisioned with both “workspace admin” access and API credentials to the Workspace API. This will be used to query the API and can information on workspace configuration and entitlements.
Below is an excerpt from a conversation with Zach:
Hey, got a question for you:

I have code that uses the Databricks Python SDK to query the Workspace API. In order to that, it defaults to authenticating to the API using the identity of the Service Principal that's running the job; however, I could pass in different credentials (using DB secrets) if I wanted to. Whichever SP I use has to be permissioned with access to the API.
Do you think it would make more sense to:
# Permission each global STL runner SP against the API for their particular workspace
# Create a specific SP for each workspace whose credentials I explicitly invoke to query the API
# Create a different SP other than the Global STL Runner to run these specific jobs
# Something else I haven't thought of
hmm. let me think about that. need to consider where the risk sits in each case under a breach. options 2 and 3 are the same under Keyera's current security requirements.
so its a decision between does the ETL runner SP get access to the API or does a separte SP
Ok so if we are going to follow the general pattern it will be a combination of 1 and 2.
First off there is a different SP runner for every source system. the global one is only used for gold. So you will have a {{SP Extraction Databricks
column2: <workspace>}} service principal. That SP then has the ACLs for read access on the secret scope that stores the credentials for accessing the source application. The credentials would then be tied to a different databricks SP.

column1: Now the second SP seems redundant b/c Databricks is the source system in this case, but there is something to be said about sticking to a pattern. It also allows you to manage the 2nd SPs ACLs independently of the runner which is helpful.

All that said, I am still a bit wary of the level of auth being provided to that SP that has access to Databricks. I don't like the idea of it having any broad write style permissions, even on the workspace. Seems risky and would be something that would draw attention in the cyber world if they were to catch wind.
Basically, if that SP has workspace admin, then it can run other jobs and gain access to the secrets that the other SPs have access to.

I'm also curious how you are able to get all the information you need when each SP is only scoped to a single workspace? or are you thinking an job runs in prod but is attached to an SP that has workspace rights on all workspaces?
Ok, this sounds like a good pattern (if super freakin' involved - lol).

I share your concerns regarding access. I don't think that the SP that queries the API (or, as DB prefers, uses the Python SDK) would need Workspace Admin permissions because it doesn't need to write anything to the API, it just needs to read data.

I haven't found any information on how to set scopes (not Secret Scopes) through either the API or the SDK, so I am thinking that since the SDK authenticates using OAuth, it might restrict access based on what the SP is permissioned on. That said, to list all groups and read their entitlements, maybe that does require Workspace Admin access. I honestly don't know.
ya permissions will be what the SP has been assigned in that case
it will just depend on the entitlements needed to get that data
Ok, confirmed. What SP is calling the API needs to be a workspace admin to get the necessary entitlement and membership info.
hmm. ok. that's not ideal. we will need to review  the data you are trying to access before it leaves PoC and see if there is another way to get you the same information without that level of access.
otherwise we'll get yelled at by cyber security and lose all the good will we have built up over the last year.
Yeah. It seems like the workspace entitlements data isn't available anywhere else.

So, one thing we could potentially do...I know that the way we have defined ""Workspace Admin"" groups includes a ton of emergency data access. But this SP doesn't need ANY data access. They just need to be part of the ""admins"" group for their workspace. Now, that obviously gives them some power, but I don't think that it gives them the ability to do things like create clusters and on it's own it doesn't give them any data access.

It's less privilege than the CI/CD SP, which already has admin rights.",,Scott Drennan,,,,,,,,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@33053909,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

Currently, the {{publish_sample_data}} Glue job exports samples from the MMS database to an S3 table named {{sample_analysis_data}}. This job operates on a rolling 30-day window based on the sample's creation date. As a result, any sample created more than 30 days ago is excluded from updates in the S3 table even if it has been modified in MMS.
For accurate reporting, we need to eliminate this 30-day window constraint and present data in a table so that it reflects the current state of all samples in MMS, regardless of their creation date.

I've noticed there are many duplicates occurring in the production daily volumes table. We have corrected any duplicate data from MMS at the source by deleting duplicate entries. These should be left out in the daily production volumes dashboard since we don't include any 'deleted' records there. However, I am wondering if there is a transformation step that is causing an amplification of duplicates between the final measurement data table and the daily production volume - last 14 months table.  For example, we have a duplicate *KFS_FQ_115.PDAY_MSS* record on *2025-07-10* appearing 8 times, and they all have a status of 'Validated-System'. These duplicates do not appear in any other table/AWS bucket or in MMS, as far as I have found.  If you have the time to look into why we are getting so many duplicates that would be fantastic.

* Complete implementation of Terraform for IaC (Infrastructure-as-Code) deployment

** Terraform is used with Databricks to define and deploy our workspaces, data catalogs, business domain data schemas, primary service principals, groups, all-purpose compute, compute policies, SQL warehouses, and to apply security permissions to all of the above.

** Similar to Databricks, Terraform can be used with AWS to define and deploy resources as IaC. We should be using this to deploy the underlying S3 storage, virtual private clusters, and virtual private network assets for our Databricks environments.

** Databricks includes the ability to define groups, users, and service principals with fine-grained access permissions. However, it lacks built-in tools to effectively manage these objects and permissions,

** This is a collection of notebooks, jobs, tables, and dashboards intended to validate that our system’s groups, users, and service principals, and their associated security permissions, conform to our expected state (as defined in the Terraform above). These will allow us to 1. validate that the Terraform configuration is correct, 2. detect whether any changes have been made since a Terraform deployment (either by jobs or manually), and 3. maintain a history of our IAM posture, which will improve our ability to audit access and investigate any issues.

** Databricks includes robust logging of almost all system events and writes those logs to system tables. However, it does not have built-in tools to analyze those logs and surface potentially concerning items. It also does not maintain this history for more than 1 year.

** This will be a library of scripts that will define potentially concerning activity, parse the system logs, and flag any items that we specify. We can also use this code base to store relevant audit logs within our own AWS storage, ensuring that we meet Keyera’s data retention policies.
* Implement DR, Backup, and Archival Patterns
** We need to define and implement our disaster recovery, source data backup, and result data archival patterns.
** This needs to include DR plans for IaC code, ETL code, virtual infrastructure fail-over, and backup of S3.

** We currently use multiple patterns for ingestion of data from source systems (e.g., SQL CDC, DMS CDC, direct query, API query). This is not necessarily an issue and is – to some extent – unavoidable. However, it does increase complexity and may also increase costs. We should consider future work to normalize our ingestion patterns, where and when it makes sense.

** The Commercial Solutions workspaces were created as part of a separate Databricks pilot conducted with Arcurve. It has always been the plan to decommission these workspaces and merge their content into the Data Extraction and Analytics Lakehouse workspaces. This will free up workspace quota, reduce cost, and dramatically simplify system management.
* Integration of all ETL into Primary Code Base

** At present there are multiple distinct code bases handling ETL tasks: keyera-databricks, keyera-emissions, keyera-measurement, and (to a lesser extent) databricks-admin. We should consolidate all ETL code into a single code base to improve maintainability, transparency, and control.
* Configuration of Power BI as Presentation Layer
** We need to more fully investigate and possibly configure Power BI since the business uses it as their preferred presentation layer.

** Our code is documented with docstrings and readme files. OS BD
OS BD Team requires an all-encompassing report that summarizes its performance in relation to customers volume with the FSCS product system. The OS BD team requires eONE data to:
# Track customer volumes and revenue to improve strategy/commercial relations
# Prepare annual budgets, 5-year forecasts, expected volumes, expected revenues
# Access/visibility to daily volumetric data to track production against the budget/plan
Data examples are stored in the ‘Oilsands Data Integration Breakdown’ shared with Melanie, Gladys, and Lee. Data table requests listed by priority and accessibility:

# ‘Keyera Account Journal Qbyte Detail’ ingestion – this report provides key financial information based on the contracted volumes OS customers are receiving monthly. The table also has key columns (Resp cost Center Qbyte) to connect eONE data to the Qbyte system, allowing an in-depth analysis on asset performance margins.

# ‘Product Inventory” Workflow ingestion – provides further breakdown on the customer contracts, providing nuances to each individual contract additional fees or make up rights that is not represented in the rolled-up Account Journal. Key items provide OS BD with intel on opportunities to increase fees, improving revenue.

# ‘C5 Daily Balance’ (unable to source as it sits on the logistics side) - is an excel logistics manually fills in and inputs into eONE with volumes by customer by receipt/delivery point. This data would be the key for strategic planning as it will provide BD with knowledge of the upstream supply Keyera is currently capturing (market capture).
* Quality volume and financial data from eONE, Qbyte and MMs/QQ
* Be able to identify but not limited to the 14 receipt points and 7 delivery points in eONE and MMs/QQ (MMS 75% verified)
* Validate customer specific data including volumes flowing through each receipt/delivery point (eONE from the logistics side)
* Access to the required data to prepare:
** Power Bi dashboard – includes identification of volume flows by customer, revenue by customer and OPEX
** Ability to measure monthly customer volumes
** Ability to link volume flow to contract fee for Keyera Corp.
# KPLI – Keyera Account Journal QByte Detail report

The Logistics team currently uses a Power BI report called “Daily Facility Balance” to monitor daily storage volumes by commodity and customer. The current process for data ingestion is a three-step workflow:
# Schedulers manually input the data into eOne.
# IT has set up an automated export of the eOne report, which is sent to the Logistics service account mailbox in CSV format.
# A Power Automate flow uploads the CSV to a SharePoint folder, from which Power BI pulls the data.

While functional, this process is manual and prone to delay. We're now looking to leverage Databricks to streamline data access and automate the flow of KFS Frac & Storage Facility volumetric data into a historical dataset. The goal is to create a more efficient, scalable, and automated reporting pipeline.

column3: A list of parties, including their addresses, involved in a rail shipments - customers, consignees, care-of, importers, exporters, freight payors, customs payors, customs brokers, etc.
A list of contracts between Keyra and Customers for rail shipments. Only Propane contracts included. The list in Geo is sourced from eOne deals.

A list of routes available to use for rail shipments orders. A route for rail shipments is a data structure that includes essential details about product movement, such as origin, destination, railroads and junctions, product, consignee, freight payment terms, and payors.

A list of orders for product movement. An order is a request for specific product movement, detailing the loading month, number of railcars, shipper, product, facility, route, and additional parties of interest (such as care of, importer, exporter, customs broker, payor, notify party). It also includes contracts, export permits, embargo information, instructions for facilities, and Order Status

A list of shipments for each order. A shipment is a record creted in Geo for each car on the Order. Each Order Detail contains information about shipments dates (planned, scheduled, shipped), shipment status, physical railcar assigned, name of BOL file generated for the shipment
Bill of Lading documents in pdf format for cars shipped

Following Wallena Kendericks's request that *all front-end data be accessed digitally—similar to how KFS front-end is connected to their DCS/Historian*—we have a new ask to ensure that front-end users no longer need to manually upload or download data from Databricks. This initiative is designed to streamline daily accounting, BD, and logistics processes by integrating the necessary data directly into Excel. Our goal is to build a comprehensive, digitally accessible dataset that improves efficiency and supports self-service analytics.
*Note:* We are not supporting direct querying of Databricks from Excel for non-developers. Excel should connect to a Power BI Semantic Model that draws from Databricks.
Walina Kendrick and Dean Brunce - the person to contact for additional details
This will need to go through the Intake Process for Data Foundations

How will be doing this task?

* The schema of the MMS data was updated in AWS, but these changes are not being reflected in the Unity Catalog explorer view in Databricks,
* However, queries that use the updated schema still run successfully,
* But the explorer and SQL editor show schema mismatch or error highlights.
To help investigate further, could you please provide the following:
# Updated schema definition (ideally before vs after, if available)
# Exact steps to reproduce the issue
# Actual vs expected behavior (especially in the explorer and SQL editor)
Also, please confirm if this is a blocking issue.

Correct. In the keyera-commercial-prod workspace we have created an external location to an S3 location (s3://mms-datapipeline-prod-ca-central-1-844580754610-validated/sample_analysis_data) in the *keyera-prod-mms* AWS account.

Using Athena to view that schema, you can see the sample_analysis_date table. I do not have a previous screenshot, but it was changed to include “sample_point_name” after it was initially setup as an external location. When this change happened, the schema in Databricks did (and has not) updated. However, if you run a query using sample_point_name it successfully complete.

*This is not a blocking issue*. I just wanted to capture it as it looks like weird Databricks behaviour, and might be a bug on their side vs. something the team can fix short of re-creating the external location.

_What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?_

_A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption._
_Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:_
{quote}🚫 _“I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”_
(/) _“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”_{quote}
h2. What is the value of solving this problem?
_What is the value of solving the problem? Wherever possible, provide a statement of tangible and quantifiable business value._
h2. What is/isn’t the urgency tied to solving this problem?

_Why is or isn’t this work urgent? Provide an explanation for why the work must be completed as soon as possible or by a specific deadline. Note: Adding a requirement here does not guarantee that the work will be done by a certain date, but the explanation provided will assist in prioritization._
_How will we solve this problem with data?_
_What are the specific deliverables? See the “Define” story for more on capturing requirements._","_The following information is necessary to complete setup of the business and data access packages:_

Objective

Enable business users to access unvalidated, raw production volume data earlier in the day so they can begin working with it before MMS validation is complete. This is achieved by enhancing the existing {{gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months}} table and introducing a supporting pipeline that stages and updates tag data progressively.
h3. Step 0: Create External Table Over AWS S3
* Point it directly to the AWS S3 bucket in the *Q2 account* where raw measurement data is stored.
* Avoid any transformations at this stage — the table should reflect the raw schema and structure of the source files.
* Ensure the table includes a {{data_load_time}} column to support downstream filtering.
* Create a new table or view named {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_2_days}}.
* This table will serve as the authoritative source for recent unvalidated tag data and will be used in downstream logic.
* Update the logic of this existing table to incorporate tag data from:
*** Use the {{status}} value provided by MMS (e.g., {{""Validated-System/Reviewed/etc""}}).
*** Use the {{status}} column already assigned in Step 1 ({{""UNVALIDATED""}}).
*** If there is a validated volume from MMS from that tag, take the MMS volume over the unvalidated tag volume.
* Modify the existing Databricks job named *Daily Production Volumes* to:
** Include logic for ingesting and processing data from {{silver_volumetrics.unvalidated_last_7_days}}.
** Run every 15 minutes between 07:00 and 09:00 local time.

** Update {{gold_volumetrics.daily_production_volumes_last_fourteen_months}} with the latest tag data and statuses.",,Lee Pattison,Pauline Telan,Scott Drennan,Svetlana Garaev,,,,,61d60cf3e7637900680e44d0,6230ae1375f257006a99beed,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,557058:df742dde-c297-4b5d-b42f-35d95bc257de,,,,,,,,,,,,,DF-485,DF-400,,DF-487,DF-686,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,DF-556,DF-121,,,,,,,,,,,16/Jul/25 1:24 PM;ug:390014ce-9eeb-4986-a91b-cbe63aff77da;Unvalidated Volumes Test Scripts and Results.docx;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/27046,17/Jul/25 10:27 AM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;image-20250717-162544.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/27062,17/Jul/25 10:27 AM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;image-20250717-162719.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/27064,17/Jul/25 10:27 AM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;image-20250717-162726.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/27063,07/Aug/25 11:06 AM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;image-20250807-170432.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/27334,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@303b8ae5,,,,,0.0,,"{pullrequest={dataType=pullrequest, state=MERGED, stateCount=2}, json={""cachedValue"":{""errors"":[],""summary"":{""pullrequest"":{""overall"":{""count"":2,""lastUpdated"":""2025-07-15T14:30:17.950-0600"",""stateCount"":2,""state"":""MERGED"",""dataType"":""pullrequest"",""open"":false},""byInstanceType"":{""bitbucket"":{""count"":2,""name"":""Bitbucket Cloud""}}}}},""isStale"":true}}",,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

column1: ** _What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?_
** _What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?_
** _What sources have the data that we think is needed?_

** _How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?_
** _Who is the audience for the data?_

This is the collection point for tracking work items and development.,https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/,Medium,,Gladys Salas,5e21f5382f2d9a0ca50d3770,Tania Nezic,61fd8615f51e8500708a4414,Scott Drennan,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,19/Jun/25 10:04 AM,17/Sep/25 12:34 PM,,,,,,,,,,,,,0,Measurement,,,,"* *Business Owner:* Tyson van Leusden
_What is the business problem that we are trying to solve with data?_

_A “data product” is a package of work that results in one or more related data sets that are available to data analysts and/or business consumers. Most often, a data product will require work related to definition, ingestion, transformation, processing, and consumption._
_Rather than being defined by tables in a source system, data products should be defined by deliverables that are tied to some business capability. For example:_
{quote}🚫 _“I want the data from 13 tables in Qbyte so that I can query the data for my report.”_
(/) _“I want to create a dashboard for our PMO, to support our Source-to-Pay effort by showing how cloud infrastructure costs relate to our project portfolio.”_{quote}
h2. What is the value of solving this problem?
_What is the value of solving the problem? Wherever possible, provide a statement of tangible and quantifiable business value._
* Allows for joining measurement data to other data sets for wider usage.
* Combines measurement data with business context.
* Publishes measurement data to wider audiences.
h2. What is/isn’t the urgency tied to solving this problem?
Volumetric data is fundamental to all business lines and to enabling our analysts.
_How will we solve this problem with data?_
* We need to provide timely access to a variety of measurement data sets, especially:
* In addition to the raw datasets, we will also make broad data available through Databricks Dashboards and via Power BI semantic models.
_What are the specific deliverables? See the “Define” story for more on capturing requirements._
# Delivery of “raw” volume data - incorporate previous day PDAY (production day) tagged data from AWS MMS Raw data store to enable the use of daily data in nominations processes.
## Incorporation of the raw data into the Production Volumes Databricks Dashboard
## Replacement of raw data with validated data once available

# Access to balance data - so that we can streamline (and not recalculate) providing balance group data and flow weighted average sample date. (60 Day history - verify [~accountid:6230ae1375f257006a99beed])

# Delivery of curated volume data tables - the existing “gold_volumetrics” tables are too large and have variable granularity (minute, hour, day data is mixed). We must undertake data analysis and determine a set of more curated gold tables to increase usability.
# Other Compositional Data - for Measurement Quality Team Reporting & Logistics use. Includes:
# Translate the queries behind the Measurements Dashboard into gold tables so the curated data can be used by PA and other audiences.
# Ingest relational information (e.g., meter and sample point) from MMS PostgreSQL database.

# Possibly create component balancing table POC in sandbox - [~accountid:61d60d71a54af900697ee9aa] ","_The following information is necessary to complete setup of the business and data access packages:_
* What is the sensitivity classification of the data (Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential)?
* Who is the business owner (1-2 specific individuals)?
* Who is the business steward (1-2 specific individuals)?
* Who are the business approvers (1-2 specific individuals)? _Usually the same as business steward._
* What Power BI workspace does this data need to be available in?

This is the collection point for tracking work items and development.,https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/,Medium,,Mike Hughesman,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,Mike Hughesman,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,Mike Hughesman,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,18/Jun/25 1:34 PM,17/Sep/25 12:34 PM,,,,,,Data Storefront,,,,,,,0,,,,,"*DESCRIPTION*

Create process documentation to facilitate the integration to support the addition, update, and removal of SCIs (Service Catalog Items). This process may be automated or manual depending on the scope and complexity of the task.  I would suggest we focus on manual process and convert that to an automated process should we have the resources to do so. The goal is to ensure accurate and timely synchronization of SCI data between DUC+ and FreshService to support service management workflows.
This enhancement improves data consistency and operational efficiency in configuration management.
* The integration process supports adding, updating, and removing SCIs in FreshService based on the content of the DUC+.
* Manual and automated processes are clearly defined and documented.
* SCI changes are logged and auditable.
* SCI management for systems not tracked in DUC+.
* Enhancements to DUC+ or FreshService outside of SCI synchronization.
* API or data access to DUC+ and FreshService.
* Defined SCI data model and mapping rules.
* Authentication and authorization for integration endpoints.
* Ensure compliance with Keyera’s configuration management and audit policies.
* Include error handling and alerting for failed sync operations.

* This enhancement lays the groundwork for broader CMDB automation.",,Mike Hughesman,,,,,,,,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@36931f2,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

This is the collection point for tracking work items and development.,https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/,Medium,,Jordan Richter,712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf,Mike Hughesman,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,Mike Hughesman,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,18/Jun/25 1:21 PM,17/Sep/25 12:34 PM,,,,,,Data Storefront,,,,,,,0,,,,,"*DESCRIPTION*

Enhance the Orchestration Server to execute scripts that configure access to approved security groups. These scripts will be triggered by upstream workflow approvals (e.g., from FreshService) and will automate the provisioning of access entitlements based on predefined rules and mappings.
This enhancement supports scalable, policy-driven access management and reduces manual effort in provisioning tasks.
* The Orchestration Server can execute scripts that apply access configurations to security groups.
* Scripts are parameterized and support logging, error handling, and rollback where applicable.
* Manual access provisioning or approval workflows.
* Integration with systems not included in the approved access scope.
* Access to target systems and services (e.g., AD, application APIs).
* Secure execution environment for script operations.
* Ensure all scripts follow Keyera’s security, audit, and change control policies.
* Include retry logic and alerting for failed or partial executions.

* This enhancement is a foundational step toward full automation of access provisioning workflows.",,Jordan Richter,Mike Hughesman,,,,,,,712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@509e188e,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

column1: with that out of the way, the current functionalities for scripting are as follows:
* Add to AD Group (Simple.Add to AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to add the user to the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
** invalid user/group (hard with prior validation, but it’s possible nonetheless)
** other AD-related errors (e.g. service account doesn’t have permissions to modify the given security group)
* Remove from AD Group (Simple.Remove from AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to remove the user from the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
** invalid user/group (hard with prior validation, but it’s possible nonetheless)
** lack of existing admission to group
** other AD-related errors (e.g. service account doesn’t have permissions to modify the given security group)
* Add to Azure AD Group (Simple.Add to Azure AD Group.ps1) - taking in passed username and AD group, it will attempt to add the user to the specified group. Errors accounted for include:
the main functionality we’ve added is the SCIMapping.ps1 file and Search-SCI function contained within the Common.Magic Spells.psm1 file.

# SCIMapping provides a layer of security (requested by Mike Hughesman) that obfuscates the full security group until it reaches the server. This file creates a reference look-up key-value pair where the partial group name sent from FS is then translated to the full group for the file
# the Search-SCI function uses the above mapping file to complete the look-up to the proper security group

*NOTE:* the Convert-HtmlTableToPowerShellObject function is currently commented out as while the functionality works if the file is run on the server, it’s not working through FS. as no tickets currently have fields, we have not found the need to enable this at this time","04/Jul/25 10:11 AM;712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf;A bit more info about the added code.

Enhance FreshService by establishing a standardized (as best we can) set of workflows and automations to process every Service Catalogue Item (SCI) consistently. These workflows will streamline the handling of FreshService requests and ensure that each SCI follows a predictable, auditable process from submission to fulfillment.
This enhancement supports automation, reduces manual intervention, and improves service delivery consistency.
* A defined workflow exists for each SCI in FreshService.
* Workflows include steps such as approval routing, group assignment, and ticket resolution.
* Automations are configured to trigger based on SCI-specific criteria (e.g., product type, requester role).
* Notifications are sent to relevant stakeholders at key stages (e.g., request received, approved, fulfilled).
* Each workflow logs actions for audit purposes.
* Errors or exceptions in workflow execution are logged and surfaced to administrators.
* Manual ticket handling outside of defined workflows.
* Integration with external systems beyond FreshService (unless explicitly required by the SCI).
* Access to FreshService admin console for workflow configuration.
* Defined business rules for each SCI’s fulfillment process.
* Consider using FreshService’s workflow automator and scenario automations for implementation.
* Align workflows with existing ITSM practices and compliance requirements.

* This enhancement lays the groundwork for scalable, automated access provisioning.",,Jordan Richter,Mike Hughesman,,,,,,,712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf,712020:6893c53e-0a1a-4b92-bc57-83ae6941b487,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,07/Jul/25 3:55 PM;712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf;image-20250707-203148.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/26915,07/Jul/25 3:55 PM;712020:2feb8a1e-46c6-4314-a459-e9a6f33746cf;image-20250707-203154.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/26916,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@4fc45162,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

Automate the retrieval of FreshService service catalog items by configuring the Data Storefront to perform a daily GET request at 5:30 AM from FreshService. The response, a flat file containing the catalog data, will be stored in a designated folder accessible to the Data Menu for processing and display.
* A scheduled job runs daily at 5:30 AM to perform a GET request to the FreshService API.
* The API call retrieves the full list of service catalog items in flat file format (JSON).
* The file is saved to a predefined folder accessible by the Data Menu.
* The job logs success/failure status and any relevant metadata (e.g., timestamp, file size).
* Errors in the API call or file write process are logged and trigger alerts.
* There is no predefined requirement for how to do the integration.
* Parsing or transforming the catalog data for display.
* FreshService API credentials and endpoint access.
* File storage location with read access for the Data Menu.
* Scheduling infrastructure (e.g., cron job, task scheduler, or cloud function).
* Ensure the job handles API rate limits and retries gracefully.
* Consider versioning or timestamping the saved files for traceability.

* Each entry includes key details: product name, request date, status, and ticket ID (if applicable).
* The list is sorted by most recent request by default.
* Clicking or expanding an entry optionally expands or links to more detailed request information.
* If no requests exist, a friendly empty state message is shown.
* Errors in loading the list are logged and surfaced to the user with a clear message.
* Editing or canceling existing tickets from the receipt list.
* Displaying tickets submitted by other users or on behalf of other users

* Authentication context to identify the current user.
* UI component library support for list rendering and empty states.

I built three main components working together: a backend API endpoint, frontend data processing, and intelligent service matching. On the backend, I created a GET route {{/api/service-catalog/requests}} that fetches tickets from Freshservice using the existing authentication credentials and HTTPS agent configuration, querying tickets for a specific user email with workspace filtering. I designed the frontend RequestReceipts component to load data from two sources simultaneously - fetching real-time ticket data from my backend API and loading the local services.json file containing the complete service catalog. The core challenge I faced was matching ticket data with service descriptions since Freshservice tickets don't contain direct service IDs. I solved this by parsing the ticket subject line, which follows the format ""Request for [user] : [service_name]"", extracting the service name and matching it against the service catalog by name. This approach allows me to enrich each ticket with detailed service information including descriptions, display IDs, and metadata. I implemented proper status mapping for Freshservice status codes (2=Open, 3=Pending, 4=Resolved, 5=Closed, 6=Pending Approval) with corresponding color coding for visual distinction. I designed the UI with a modern two-panel layout featuring filtering capabilities, where I parse service names and display them in a hierarchical format (Domain
column2: Service Type) while filtering out generic role terms like ""Business Users"" and ""Everyone"" for cleaner presentation. However, to complete this data product, we need to extend and modify the tables we are ingesting.
* Table: QRMTIPS.QCTRL_PLANT_HDR – This table has plant names associated to plant codes.

_Ingestion covers connecting to source systems, creating bronze tables and extracting data into those tables, cleaning the data, and loading it into silver tables. Note: It does not include the application of business logic or the creation of gold tables._

_Please provide a description of the source systems and the tables that will be ingested, along with any technical requirements._ *_If the Data Product requires more than one source system or requires multiple steps to connect and stage the data, we may need to create more than one story._* _Use the questions below to guide your work._
* _What source systems are we ingesting from?_
* _What method are we using to connect to those systems?_

* _Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?_
* _What is the structure of the source system data?_
* _Are there data quality considerations that need to be overcome?_
* _What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?_

* _How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?_",,Scott Drennan,Svetlana Garaev,,,,,,,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,557058:df742dde-c297-4b5d-b42f-35d95bc257de,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@3bb1054f,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

column1: ** _What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?_
** _What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?_
** _What sources have the data that we think is needed?_
** _What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?_

** _Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?_
** _What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?_
** _How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?_
** _Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?_
** _Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?_
** _Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?_
** _How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?_
** _Who is the audience for the data?_
** _Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?_

** _How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?_",,Scott Drennan,,,,,,,,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,DF-486,DF-487,DF-488,DF-497,DF-508,DF-509,DF-510,DF-519,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@2b05ad01,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

TIPS contains a separate table per code type, each table including the code itself, its description and - in most cases - the last updated time stamp. This data can be presented to users as a set of tables of a similar structure (Code, Code Description, Last Update), or as one table, with an additional column for a a code type (Code Type, Code, Code Description, Last Update). The main use of this data is to help users work with TIPS data.
Potentially, this data can be used by other TIPS data products, for resolving codes to their names/descriptions.

column1: Gold 7: TIPS to Q2 Meter Mapping Table,DF-379,38568,Story,In Evaluation,DF,Data Foundations,software,Lee Pattison,61d60cf3e7637900680e44d0,Jira Project space for the Data Foundations project. This is the collection point for tracking work items and development.,https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/,Medium,,Zackary Oleitschuk,712020:c79871b4-3321-48a4-b4ae-d1a84eb31c0b,Svetlana Garaev,557058:df742dde-c297-4b5d-b42f-35d95bc257de,Svetlana Garaev,557058:df742dde-c297-4b5d-b42f-35d95bc257de,16/Jun/25 1:46 PM,18/Sep/25 11:56 AM,,,,G&P BD TIPS v1,,Data Validation / QA,Environment Management,Requirements Definition,,,,,0,BD,G&P,,,"As a Business Development (BD) Rep, I need to map TIPS meters to Q2 daily volume tags so that I can reconcile meter data from these two applications.

TIPS and Q2 meters are the same physical meters, but known under different names in those applications and associated with different data elements: TIPS provides customer allocation on meters, and Q2 provides volume and composition on the same meters. Upon reconciling the meter data, BDs can estimate allocated month-to-date volumes (with composition) to customer, before these volumes are posted in TIPS. This data will be presented in [Customer Volume Projection

For the purpose of this initiative, we only need to map the unique ID of a TIPS meter to the unique ID of the same meter in Q2. However for usability, the mapping needs to be enhanced with meter properties from each app, such as plant, product, parent device, description etc. To avoid the “garbage-in” situation, TIPS meter properties can be retrieved from the Meter Hierarchy table ({{keyera_enterprise_prod.gold_tips.meter_hierarchy}}) in Databricks. Q2 meter properties can be retrieved from MMS tables (public.measurement_tag and public.measurement_tag_suffix).
# Create a gold TIPS-Q2 meter mapping table in Databricks, as per product definition: [https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/87687169/TIPS-Q2+Meter+Mapping
column3: smart-link]. Also, there is a mock-up destination table with TIPS-Q2 data mapping here : {{keyera_temporary.sandbox.tips_q2_mapping_manual}}. Please note that the table is not exact, just a rough draft. Use the product definition in Confluence as a final reference.

column1: Including “Keyera” in the names follows common cloud standards, ensures globally unique identifiers, and helps future-proof resources for scenarios like mergers/acquisitions/joint ventures or data sharing. More importantly, Databricks workspaces cannot be renamed in place; renaming would require full recreation and migration of all assets, including some AWS resources.
Given the high cost and risk compared to the limited benefit, keeping the current naming convention is the most practical approach.
That said, we can do this. I just don’t think it aligns with the direction you want to be going.

We must document technical standards for the integration of Power BI with Databricks. This should include:
* Use of Service Principals in DB
* Use of Service Accounts in PBI (or not)
* Version control on Power BI reports (Dhruv)
* Use of deployment pipelines in Power BI (or not) (Dhruv)
* Access control Power BI workspaces and apps (Dhruv)
* Credential management and Personal Access Tokens
* Best practices related to Native Queries vs. mCode vs. Dax (Dhruv)
* Best practices related to Direct Query vs. Import (Dhruv)
* Controls on other Fabric funtions (like Dataflows, data warehouse, etc.) - i.e. Where should work occur?
* Best practices on use of paginated reports
* Licencing for Power BI (pro users vs. premium workspaces) (Dhruv)
* Guidelines on access non-databricks sources directly from Power BI
* Use of Power BI vs. Databricks Dashboards
* Connection of Excel to Semantic Models (Dhruv)
* What services do we offer in Power BI?
* Access Control & Networking Security with Power BI & Databricks (get reference from Dhruv)
* Roles in workspaces in Power BI (Dhruv)
_Note: This story does not include How-To documentation. Please capture needed or recommended how-to documentation elsewhere._

A new Data Analyst or platform admin is able to consult our technical standards and setup a new workspace within Power BI, connect it to Databricks, and allow for local development of reports and successful publishing of the report to the Power BI service.

_Note: All technical standard documentation must be reviewed and approved prior to being considered “done.”_",,Dhruv Modi,Scott Drennan,,,,,,,712020:3c1bf772-ab2c-4358-82e5-e53cb9bc2bca,712020:32c2239a-0e07-4ec9-9631-3c8768666b03,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@71a195e,,,,,0.0,,{},,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

Each major section should be its own story.
* General Architecture Principles and Best Practices
** Power BI is used for visualization.
** Data modelling and transformation should be done as much as possible in Databricks.
** We are BI agnostic. People can use Databricks Dashboards, Power BI, Visual KPI, Tableau, SAP BO, etc.
* Technical Standards for Integration with Power BI
** Use of Service Principals in DB
** Use of Service Accounts in PBI (or not)
** Version control on Power BI reports
** Use of deployment pipelines in Power BI (or not)
** Access control Power BI workspaces and apps
** Credential management and Personal Access Tokens
** Best practices related to Native Queries vs. mCode vs. Dax
** Best practices related to Direct Query vs. Import
** Controls on other Fabric funtions (like Dataflows, data warehouse, etc.) - i.e. Where should work occur?
** Best practices on use of paginated reports
** Licencing for Power BI (pro users vs. premium workspaces)
** Guidelines on access non-databricks sources directly from Power BI
** Use of Power BI vs. Databricks Dashboards
** Connection of Excel to Semantic Models
** What services do we offer in Power BI?
** Access Control & Networking Security with Power BI & Databricks (get reference from Dhruv)
** Report refresh cadence (Databricks Dashboards or external)
** AWS S3 Storage per team sandbox schema
** Ingestion patterns from souce landscape and decision tree
*** Use of Developer Accounts for Data Analysis (as opposed to service accounts)
*** Import whole database and whole tables
** Use of Entra / Active Directory Groups
** Single Service Account per App / Purpose

This was causing conflict issues in the deployment pipeline (screenshot #1) as it couldn’t seem to write the old jsons into the keyera-databricks-emissions-dev/files/dashboards folder. After deleting the old dashboard jsons in dev and manually redeploying, it fixed the issue. After running the pipeline however it now imports all the old lvdash.json files as dashboards, clogging up the Dashboards screen (screenshot #2). To fix this, we’ve decided to delete the old _vx.lvdash.json from the source code and rely on Git to restore previous versions.

We have large numbers of contracts and amendments that we need to understand and analyze in aggregate.

column1: ** What data do we think we need to solve the business problem?
** What other factors besides data might need to be addressed to solve the problem?
** What sources have the data that we think is needed?
** What are the characteristics of the source data that we need to be aware of (e.g., refresh cadence, quality, granularity)?

** Are the data sources relatively easy to access or do they require extra development to connect (e.g., is it an internal system with an accessible database, does it have an object model that makes it difficult to query, do we need to pull the data from an API and do we have access)?
** What is the shape of the source data and what shape is needed in the final product?
** How clean is the source data and does it conform to Keyera standards (e.g., quality, units of measure)?
** Does the data need to be normalized or joined with other data sets to be useful?
** Is the source data already well understood, or does it require exploration and manipulation by a senior data analyst?
** Is a single set of final “gold” tables sufficient, or is there value in providing access to some intermediate date sets?
** How will the data be used (e.g., internal analysis, machine learning, presentation to end users)?
** Who is the audience for the data?
** Does the data include sensitive or confidential information?

** How does the business intend to consume the data (e.g., Excel, Power BI, Databricks Dashboard, or will it feed into another system)?","_The following information is necessary to complete setup of the business and data access packages:_
* What is the sensitivity classification of the data (Public, Internal, Confidential, Highly Confidential)?
* Who is the business owner (1-2 specific individuals)?
* Who is the business steward (1-2 specific individuals)?
* Who are the business approvers (1-2 specific individuals)? _Usually the same as business steward._

column2: https://keyera.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DF/pages/22642780/Wapiti+Testing+Log] for data issues encountered so far. This story is aiming to address most if not all the issues encountered in the log so that these types of issues do not happen again.

column1: # Currently when the script creates a new table in bronze, it assumes the data type of all the columns. If a column is blank at the time the table is created, the ingestion script may create the column as a numeric type even though it should be a string. This is now causing some issues with the new Wapiti data as columns that were previously blank now have strings in them. Ingestion then fails because the table is expecting an integer.
# Pull all data into bronze as strings. Move data validation into silver instead.
### Pull all data as strings. Keep null values.
### Still clean column names. Current way works.
### Filter out records that have all nulls across all columns.
### Enforce null checks. e.g. if there is a null value in gas composition, set it to 0
# Recreate all the bronze and silver sharepoint tables.

What is the problem?

FCTT month end process is run manually through Excel. It starts with collecting data from Dearman, eOne and Comp Match, ensuring the sync of data across these three systems, running calculations and producing a set of customer-facing documents, and providing data on customer billing to eOne. These are manual step, time-consuming and error-prone, and includes a lot of communication and coordination of effort for Logistics, Plant Accounting and Measurements.
This data then become input into more calculations for FCTT balancing.

This process is expected to be entirely developed in EnergySys. While data EnergySys holds some of the data, it requires data intakes from Dearman, eOne and Comp Match. The processing of this data in EnergySys before it is ready for calculations is a significant effort.
h1. How will we solve it?

Using Databricks as a shared visual space for Logistics, Plant Accounting and Measurements to see data discrepancies will be a huge step towards efficiency and accuracy of the FCTT month end process. We will need to compare Dearman, eOne and Comp Match data and identify discrepancies between any critical parameters, so that each business group can participate in the investigation. The resolution of discrepancies will be done in the source systems: Dearman, eOne and Comp Match.
Users will require an ability to re-load the data on demand (for example, after correcting data in the source system), as month-end processes are time-sensitive.

Once all discrepancies are resolved, users will be able to export several data sets to EnergySys. The additional benefit of this work will be preparing the data for EnergySys. This will significantly reduce the cost, effort and risk of EnergySys development for FCTT month end.
All data has been classified as “Internal” sensitivity.

The business (Measurements) requires regular access (several times a day) to Comp Match data. Due to the residency of this data in the OT network, the access needs to be facilitated by IT. This state implies constant dependency of business users on IT resources, for whom this work is mostly a disruption. Additionally, passing the results to the business relies on multiple manual steps, such as running data queries, entering query parameters, copying and pasting data, which is error-prone. Any errors can have significant financial and reputational cost to Keyera.
h2. What is the value of resolving this problem?

Providing business users with access to this data through Databricks can resolve the above issues of business dependency, IT work overload and the risks associated with human errors. In addition to the Measurements group, this information is required by Logistics and BD groups.
h2. Why is/isn’t this work urgent?
* Long overdue promise to the business to provide them with independent data access
* Freeing IT time, currently taken to facilitate data access for the business
h1. How will we solve it?

Dashboards with graphics and lists will be created for each data set that is currently generated by IT for business users. Users will be provisioned with access to the dashboards, some with limited view-only access, others (early adopters) - with ability to create their own dashboards.

All data has been classified as “Internal” sensitivity. column1: Thank you for taking the time to meet over the past weeks and walking through some of the intent and requirements for requesting this new report from Maximo. For next steps;
# I have a current request to be provided with a one-time data pull of the table/table fields easily accessible for the fields outlined in the report

## Specifics: filtered just to ""Turnaround"" Classification and the years Jan 01, 2023- Current. - This will allow us to mockup and create all the logic for the later data cube version. Establishing buy-in & Support.
# Providing you with the screenshot (worksheet 1) in the attached request book, as well as some justification to further support this request.

The request is to access our Maximo work order reporting system so we can extract cost, schedule, and materials data for historical and current turnaround projects. I believe this integration will significantly enhance how we track and manage our projects moving forward.

Currently, we're spending considerable time manually collecting project data, which often means our stakeholders are looking at information that's already outdated by the time it reaches them. By connecting directly to Maximo, we can provide real-time visibility into job plan execution, schedule performance, and cost tracking. This means our team leaders and executives will finally have current information to make informed decisions rather than reacting to problems after they've already impacted our timelines and budgets.

What excites me most about this approach is its scalability potential. Once we establish this dashboard framework for our current projects, we can quickly roll it out to maintenance operations, capital projects, and even procurement activities. The beauty of using a standardized data structure is that we'll have consistent reporting across all departments, which will reduce training time and improve how our teams collaborate.

The strategic value here extends well beyond just better reporting. With real-time data flowing into our dashboards, we can shift from constantly putting out fires to preventing them. We'll be able to establish meaningful benchmarks at both equipment and unit levels, which will help us identify where we're performing well and where we have opportunities to improve. This kind of institutional knowledge will be invaluable for future project planning and resource allocation.
Thank you, and let me know if you have any questions!

Venting emissions comes from blanket gas, compressor seals, and analyzers.

* Note#1: In the Equip to Analysis Lookup sheet, an allocated volume method column was added. Allocated volume method = 3, denotes the Rate method which involves calculating allocated volume = rate * equip hours. This calculation is already captured in the equip_alloc_volumes table.
Venting emission pre-requisites and requirements have been added in the attached excel file. Major steps include (steps defined in the excel):
# Add the Mol weight constants to the Gas Properties tab in Sustainability Dataset
# The venting analysis groups have been added the ""meter to analysis group"" tab in the sustainability Dataset
# The total volume for the analysis group has been calculate in <workflow name> with results placed in 'keyera_sustainability_dev.silver_air_emissions_v2.equip_allocated_volumes' table (see Note #1)
# Existing schema for keyera_sustainability_dev.silver_air_emissions_v2.emissions_compositional_grouping  updated to include additional columns: *mol_weight, mass_frac_co2, mass_frac_ch4*
# Calculate the ""Mol Weight"" of each sample
# Calculate the ""Mass Fraction of C02"" for each sample
# Calculate the ""Mass Fraction of CH4"" for each sample
# Calculate c02_emissions_t with the following calculation: Analysis group allocated volume * (Mol weight / Ideal Gas Constant) * C02 Mass Fraction
# Calculate ch4_emissions_t with the following calculation: Analysis group allocated volume * (Mol weight / Ideal Gas Constant) * CH4 Mass Fraction

# Calculate co2e_emissions_t with the following calculation: (c02_emissions_t *Global Warming Potential of C02 Constant)+ (ch4_emissions_t * Global Warming Potential of CH4 Constant)",,Colton Reid,Lee Pattison,Mateo Fidabel,Pauline Telan,,,,,712020:5faab472-6a6c-4542-bd8c-49d51b278f20,61d60cf3e7637900680e44d0,712020:1019fe96-0c82-49df-a1a1-1addad717125,6230ae1375f257006a99beed,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,DF-357,,,,,DF-313,,22/May/25 8:51 AM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;Sustainability Datasets_dev.xlsx;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/26322,18/May/25 2:12 PM;ug:390014ce-9eeb-4986-a91b-cbe63aff77da;Venting Emissions Calculation v2.xlsx;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/26249,12/May/25 1:57 PM;ug:3bdaadde-f982-4e67-9eaa-a967117a2457;image-20250512-195655.png;https://keyera.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/attachment/content/26154,,,,,,,,com.atlassian.servicedesk.plugins.approvals.internal.customfield.ApprovalsCFValue@f3b446,,,,,0.0,,"{pullrequest={dataType=pullrequest, state=MERGED, stateCount=3}, json={""cachedValue"":{""errors"":[],""summary"":{""pullrequest"":{""overall"":{""count"":3,""lastUpdated"":""2025-06-13T13:51:34.081-0600"",""stateCount"":3,""state"":""MERGED"",""dataType"":""pullrequest"",""open"":false},""byInstanceType"":{""bitbucket"":{""count"":3,""name"":""Bitbucket Cloud""}}}}},""isStale"":true}}",,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,0

This will give us insight into facility operations and customer activity prior to receiving the Posted Volumes from TIPS (~6-week lag in data currently).

column1: Today, data is processed and managed by different teams and varies from asset to asset with issues arising from the following problems:
# Limited access to customer volumes trends and insights found in the verified data from the TIPS Production Accounting tool.
# Real-time asset measurement and composition data is either underutilized or not readily accessible, hindering decision-making and customer engagement.
# Repetitive and manual processes taking time away from higher value tasks.
# Absence of a streamlined solution for visualizing historical customer toll data at G&P facilities.
# No efficient way to monitor customer activity in the market, leading to a lack of strategic visibility into the total value and growth potential each customer represents to Keyera_._
* Access to accurate and timely data will enhance the competitiveness of the G&P BD and Operations team by streamlining processes, saving time, and enabling data-driven decision-making.
* Streamline G&P data management, starting with plant volumes, to enhance daily workflows and enable data-driven decision-making.
* Visualization of trends to identify opportunities for business growth.
* Provide access to data as soon as it is available
* Create consistency across all North G&P assets.
G&P BD lacks necessary insights during customer engagement; this work will assist in driving revenue and improving margins.
h1. How will we solve it?
This epic focuses on improving access to historic monthly Customer Volumes data for G&P BD. To do so, the following will be done:
* Posted Volume, deduction, and meter hierarchy data will be extracted out of TIPS and brought into Databricks
* Table and column metadata will be defined and loaded
* Governance data (data owner, data steward) will be decided upon and documented
* Security will be setup for all data products
* A business access package will be deployed for the G&P BD analyst team to give them the required toolset to interact with data in Databricks
* A Freshservice provisioning workflow will be implemented to allow people to request, and data stewards to approve, access to the data products

The current process for aggregating monthly plant volumes requires exporting multiple reports from the SAP accounting software. BD Representatives then transform this data to summarize the volumes of raw gas entering the plant, along with the processed volumes of sales gas, NGLs, water, and acid gas. Without TIPS data BD reps are do not have insight into the NGL volumes at the plant or how much each customer is bringing to the plant,

This initial work will be used as a foundation to estimate the customer’s proportion of inlet gas entering the plant daily when it is paired with QQ data (link to JIRA). This will allow for BD reps to estimate volumes using QQ data instead of having to wait 6 weeks for TIPS data.

What is the problem?

The business wants to expand reporting on emissions by building on the work done for Rimbey and expanding it to Wapiti. An in-person session at Wapiti on May 28th provides an excellent opportunity to share data the project’s work on emissions data automation with the broader organization.
Our roll out of the Rimbey and Wapiti emissions data dashboard will follow a few months of successful quantification and replication of compliance calculations.
h2. What is the value to the business if we solve this problem?

We will use the dashboards for accruals going forward, and give access to select operations personnel. Operations will be able to use near-real-time emissions metrics to run tests and pilots on efficiency and emissions reduction projects, and to make quick and informed data driven decisions. The dashboards provide more granularity for operations and supporting groups, which will continue supporting Rimbey, Wapiti, and other facilities in identifying new opportunities for more efficient operation.

This will also allow us to decommission our existing time consuming, Excel-based calculators; it will also allow us to cancel contracts with Envirosoft, as we will no longer need to replicate emissions estimates to prove their reliability for compliance.
h2. Why is/isn’t this work urgent?
This work follows on from the Rimbey emissions pilot. It is necessary to get us closer to a clear and timely picture of our emissions and related costs.

Add Wapiti data into the current emissions dashboard for automation of emissions metrics with required workflows to be presented on May 28th at Wapiti site to Operations, Maintenance, BD and Ops T teams. Overview
Schedulers (Derek Kam) complete a daily upload of raw meter volumes into EnergySys to support daily scheduling and monthly actualization.

Schedulers receive data by email from Field Measure Coordinators and enter the data into a spreadsheet. There are typically 19 records per day with fewer than 10 fields. The primary key for the data is a Meter ID field, with data following the pattern “FIT-#####”. Multiple days of records may be imported at one time. The scheduler uploads the data to EnergySys using the I 9999 workbook, and the data is populated into the Daily Raw Meter Volumes table.
An example of the existing data import worksheet has been attached to this story.

Each day, data for the previous day will be extracted from the {{keyera_measurement_prod.gold_volumetrics.final_measurement_data}} table, cleaned and processed by a notebook, and saved to a .csv file in a SharePoint location. The EnergySys file connector will watch for the file and complete the import using the existing I 9999 process. Email notifications with attached .csv files will be sent to the schedulers at each step in the process as a manual check, but manual intervention will not be required to complete the process. Email notifications must be configurable so that they can be turned off or directed to different recipients.
A sample query structure (SQL) has been attached to this story.
*Note:* Further validation of both the query and its outputs should be completed before notebook development starts.
